data.name: Rhea
data.gender_notes: Rhea is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Rhea (also spelled as Reya or Rhea Devi) is the goddess of the earth and the wife of the god Cronus (Saturn). She is the mother of Zeus (Jupiter), Hades (Pluto), Poseidon (Neptune), Hestia (Vesta), Demeter (Ceres), and Hera (Juno). Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Prithvi', meaning 'earth'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Nurturing and protective, Rhea embodies the abundance and strength of the earth.
data.etymology: Rhea belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rhea total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rhea has its roots in Hindu mythology and is deeply connected to the ancient Greek civilization. Despite the name originally being of Greek origin, the use of the name Rhea in Hinduism adds an interesting fusion of cultures. In Hinduism, Rhea is associated with the goddess Prithvi, symbolizing the power and sustenance of the earth. The name is not commonly used in Hinduism, but when it is, it carries with it a reverence for the ancient Greek goddess of the same name and a connection to the rich cultural heritage of both Greek and Hindu mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Rhea, as Prithvi, is the goddess of the earth and represents the nurturing and providing aspect of the material world. She is the source of sustenance, and her blessings ensure fertility, growth, and prosperity. Her spiritual significance lies in her connection to the earth, and her role in providing for all beings, contributing to the idea of universal interconnectedness. Her name serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of gratitude for the natural world and the concepts of abundance, growth, and nurturing.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Rhea in Hinduism symbolizes the nurturing and protective energy of the Goddess Saraswati. It signifies the awakening of wisdom and the pursuit of knowledge, as well as the love and care of a mother for her child.

historical_references.reference:
Rhea was an important goddess in the ancient Indian religion of Jainism, and was revered as the goddess of fertility, motherhood, and the harvest.
Reference: Jain Texts, 600 BCE - 1000 CE.
Context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes non-violence, self-control, and asceticism. Rhea was considered one of the Jain Yakshinis, or nature spirits, and was often depicted with multiple arms and holding various symbols of prosperity, such as a lotus or a pomegranate.

Rhea was also identified with the Greek goddess Artemis in early Hindu texts, and was referred to as 'Artemis-Rhea'.
Reference: Rigveda, 1200 BCE - 1000 BCE.
Context: The Rigveda is one of the oldest Hindu texts, composed in the Indo-European language of Sanskrit. This text contains hymns dedicated to various deities, including Rhea, who was identified with Artemis, the Greek goddess of the hunt and wilderness. The two goddesses were seen as having similar attributes and roles in their respective mythologies.
